Alex — thanks for the clear asks. Putting options below and attaching a short proposal with invoice examples.

Three practical paths we see working well for customers in this situation:

1) Staged top-up (recommended)
- Structure: split the uplift into 3 tranches over 3 months (equal units).
- Billing: amend committed units and invoice 1/3 at each month boundary; invoices reference a single amendment and linked PO.
- Upside: smooths P&L impact, preserves committed pricing for the full uplift once the amendment is signed.
- Consideration: consumption above tranches billed at standard overage rates until amendment fully active.

2) Credit-pool smoothing
- Structure: purchase a pool of credits that get consumed against overage, invoiced upfront but discounted vs. ad-hoc overage.
- Billing: one upfront invoice, smaller monthly consumption reporting.
- Upside: simpler procurement (single PO), but front-loaded cashflow.

3) Immediate annualize + pro-rate
- Structure: lock in uplift now and annualize the new commit with a pro-rated first invoice.
- Billing: one amended contract, auto-co-term to Jan 1 renewal.
- Upside: best unit economics; consideration: larger near-term invoice.

Attached: BrightLane_Proposal_2027.pdf — includes a sample 3-month invoice schedule and a line-item breakdown that finance can drop into a PO.

Next steps I suggest:
- If procurement prefers staged billing, we can draft an amendment and a 3-month invoice schedule for PO submission.
- If they prefer a single PO, credit-pool keeps things simple.

Looping in Ben for pricing guardrails and Lauren for ops/tax timing.
